bib.title: Can language models learn from explanations in context?
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2022

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; dot-matrix plot residue in Figs 6-12 not read.

question: Can explanations of few-shot examples placed in the prompt improve language-model task performance, and what drives any benefit?
hypothesis: Explanations that link examples to task principles, which help human learning, may also improve in-context learning in LMs.
contributions: Annotate 40 diverse, challenging BIG-bench tasks with explanations of examples and release them
Evaluate several LMs with or without few-shot examples, explanations, instructions and control conditions
Show explanations of few-shot examples improve large-model performance and beat matched controls even untuned
Show explanations tuned or selected on a small validation set have larger effects
Analyse with hierarchical statistical models respecting task/item/prompt dependencies

method.summary: Gopher-family decoder-only LMs (1B, 7B, 280B) are evaluated on 40 multiple-choice BIG-bench tasks under 0- and 5-shot prompts, with or without a task instruction, and with author-written post-answer explanations or matched controls. Answers are chosen by greedy highest likelihood of each option. Effects are estimated with hierarchical logistic regressions; selection and hand-tuning of explanations on a small validation set are also tested.
method.task: few-shot in-context learning on multiple-choice reasoning tasks (BIG-bench subset)

datasets.name: 40 BIG-bench tasks/subtasks (explanation annotations released)
datasets.size: 15 examples per task annotated with explanations; three 5-shot prompts per task; regression data 17,028 task:input groups (untuned model), 26,786 (selection model)
datasets.split: Evaluated on all task items except the 5 in the prompt; tuning on the other annotated examples (10 validation items for hand-tuning)
datasets.source: BIG-bench collaboration 2021 (multiple-choice JSON tasks); annotations by a single author, released at a Google Cloud Storage bucket dm_some_explanations_for_bigbench_tasks
datasets.preprocessing: Task prefixes omitted except where they carry necessary information; 5-shot prompt with instruction and explanations plus target must fit in 2048 tokens; largest model's 5-shot accuracy below 75% on all chosen tasks; causal_judgment annotations were lost, analysed only untuned on the largest model

other.training_data: same quantity of the same dataset across sizes

inference.decoding: No generation: score likelihood of each answer option given prompt and question, pick the highest greedily; no length normalisation; no prior correction (Holtzman et al. 2021 tried, no benefit in preliminary run)
inference.samples: Three 5-shot prompts per task (prompt_index; 120 prompts across 40 tasks); no repeated seeds as decoding is deterministic scoring
inference.prompting: Optional task instruction, then 0 or 5 examples separated by a blank line, each 'Q: ... A: ...' with optional 'Explanation:' line after the answer; conditions: instruction (none/instruction/non-instruction) x explanation (none/real/other-item/true non-explanation/scrambled)

parameters.controls: scrambled (word-shuffled), true non-explanation, other-item (permuted among prompt examples)
parameters.selection: greedy forward selection of 5 of the 15 annotated examples, scored on the remaining examples
parameters.hand_tuning: 5 tasks per text (4 per Table 2), start from best untuned prompt without instructions, edit on 10-example validation set

other.evaluation_hardware: Google Cloud TPU v3 (4 x 8 topology), batched inference, a few days total
other.reduced_grid: control explanations not combined with instructions or non-instructions

metrics.name: Task accuracy
metrics.definition: score defined by each BIG-bench task for the highest-likelihood option (may allow multiple correct answers or partial credit)

metrics.name: Effect size
metrics.definition: log odds ratio from hierarchical logistic regression, divided by 1.81 for Fig 2 (Chinn 2000)

metrics.name: Improvement in log score
metrics.definition: log-score difference from adding explanations vs matched prompt without

eval.protocol: Multilevel logistic regressions in R (lme4, glmer, bobyqa) with random effects for task, task:prompt_index, task:input and by-task slopes; separate models for untuned, hand-tuned and selected subsets; bootstrap 95% CIs on plots

availability.code: load_explanations.py in the data bucket (loads data and builds prompts)
availability.weights: not available; Gopher access granted to authors

prompts.purpose: Example 5-shot prompt format with instruction, example and explanation (metaphor_boolean)
prompts.text:
Answer these questions by identifying whether the second sentence is an appropriate paraphrase of the first, metaphorical sentence.
Q: David's eyes were like daggers at Paul when Paul invited his new girlfriend to dance. <- -> David had two daggers when Paul invited his new girlfriend to dance.
choice: True
choice: False
A: False
Explanation: David's eyes were not literally daggers, it is a metaphor used to imply that David was glaring fiercely at Paul.
...
Q: Our whole life we swim against the waves towards the green light of happiness. <- -> Our whole life we try to reach happiness.
choice: True
choice: False
A:

evidence.quote: We greedily choose the highest-likelihood answer from the set

results.claim: Adding untuned post-answer explanations to 5-shot prompts raises accuracy on the log-odds scale (fixed effect).
results.setup: Hierarchical logistic regression (glmer) on untuned-prompt data, Gopher-family 280B model, 40 BIG-bench tasks, 5-shot, accuracy via answer likelihood

results.claim: Few-shot examples versus zero-shot are the largest prompt effect; explanations are about a third of it.
results.setup: Hierarchical logistic regression (glmer) on untuned-prompt data, Gopher-family 280B model, 40 BIG-bench tasks, 5-shot, accuracy via answer likelihood
results.note: Text says explanations have about 1/3 the effect size of few-shot examples and twice that of instructions.

results.claim: Task instructions give a smaller benefit than untuned explanations.
results.setup: Hierarchical logistic regression (glmer) on untuned-prompt data, Gopher-family 280B model, 40 BIG-bench tasks, 5-shot, accuracy via answer likelihood

results.claim: Scrambled-word explanations hurt relative to no explanation (largest model).
results.setup: Hierarchical logistic regression (glmer) on untuned-prompt data, Gopher-family 280B model, 40 BIG-bench tasks, 5-shot, accuracy via answer likelihood

results.claim: True non-explanations have no reliable effect.
results.setup: Hierarchical logistic regression (glmer) on untuned-prompt data, Gopher-family 280B model, 40 BIG-bench tasks, 5-shot, accuracy via answer likelihood

results.claim: Other-item (permuted) explanations have no reliable effect, i.e. no better than no explanation.
results.setup: Hierarchical logistic regression (glmer) on untuned-prompt data, Gopher-family 280B model, 40 BIG-bench tasks, 5-shot, accuracy via answer likelihood

results.claim: Benefit of explanations grows with model scale: positive interaction of log parameters with explanations.
results.setup: Hierarchical logistic regression, 1B/7B/280B models, 5-shot with untuned explanations vs none

results.claim: Untuned explanations beat each control condition (relative to explanations as reference) in the largest model; scrambled is worst.
results.setup: Largest model, 5-shot, no instructions, untuned explanations as reference
results.note: Text: all other conditions worse, all beta <= -0.13, z <= -2.92, p <= 0.005.

results.claim: Selecting 5-shot examples jointly with explanations beats selecting examples alone.
results.setup: Largest model, greedy selection from 15 annotated examples per task, 40 tasks
results.note: Baseline is 'selected no explanation' 0.353198; selected with other-explanations 0.331608, true non-explanations 0.289914.

results.claim: Hand-tuned explanations give a large benefit on the hardest tasks.
results.setup: Largest model, tasks where performance was consistently low; hand-edited on a 10-example validation set
results.note: Text says five tasks were hand-tuned; Table 2 data filter lists four tasks (disambiguation_q, odd_one_out, presuppositions_as_nli, truthful_qa) and reports 4 task groups. Estimate has wide SE 0.41932.

results.claim: Condition-blind rater scored the authors' explanations as clearly explanatory.
results.setup: One question per task rated by an independent author (KM), n=38 (t(37)

results.claim: Only the largest model benefits from untuned explanations; smaller models do not.
results.setup: Gopher family 1B/7B/280B, mean accuracy across 40 tasks (read from Fig 4)
results.note: Exact accuracies only in Fig 4 (axis 40-60%); not read numerically.

limits: BIG-bench tasks are adversarially sampled and may not represent typical LM tasks; effects could be amplified or suppressed elsewhere
Single author wrote all explanations; possible bias or errors; small dataset; causal_judgment annotations lost
Only one model family (Gopher, 1B/7B/280B) with matched training; instruction-tuned or differently trained models may benefit more
Untuned benefit is modest; only the 280B model benefits untuned; smaller models might gain with more explanations or simpler tasks
Hand-tuning done on few tasks (five per text; four per Table 2), so wide CIs, bimodal gains
Selection is slightly biased vs a true validation set (hard examples avoided)
Results not comparable to published BIG-bench numbers because task prefixes were omitted
Explanations lengthen prompts and context is fixed at 2048 tokens
Post-answer explanations only; no direct comparison with pre-answer chain of thought in the same experiments
Task-cluster analysis too small to interpret strongly; 'zone of proximal development' bump is speculative
